name: Small 2-Core Components Force a Relatively Peelable Wing
statement: Under the structural and positive-section hypotheses of the one-relative-wing inverse theorem, suppose that in one exclusive wing every connected component of the graph 2-core has at most eight vertices. Then the expansion is an ample forbidden pc-minor, with no bound on the number of components or on trees attached to their 2-cores. Consequently, if neither section peels relatively to the overlap, each exclusive wing has a 2-core component on at least nine vertices.
proof: More generally, let $\varnothing\ne H\subseteq A$ have Cohen--Macaulay relative Yang module and put $D=A\setminus H$. Induct on $|D|$. A residual leaf either teaches relative to $H$, so it can be prepended after the teaching lift, or its deletion preserves Cohen--Macaulayness and it can be appended after induction. With no leaf, the relative Alexander-dual presentation splits over residual components. An isolated generator teaches; otherwise every component lies in the 2-core and has at most eight generators, so the eight-facet linear-quotients theorem supplies a teaching generator. Thus the wing has a relative ample chain, and the inverse theorem applies. The lower bound nine is the contrapositive for each wing.
